notes.detailedSummary: The fixed primary version is arXiv:2603.08664v1, submitted 9 March 2026 and internally dated 10 March. Complete pertinent definitions and proof units were read and retained. The new arguments reconstruct their geometric, convexity, envelope, and intersection dependencies independently. Theorem 4.13 was not completely read and is not applied. The essential PCC marker denotes a face relation; contact markers are grouping parentheses. The printed dossier cross obstacle has conflicting origin values and is unused. Original PDF bytes were not acquired, so recorded hashes concern actual saved response files, not the PDF.
notes.text:
Primary-source audit, not a classification theorem. Literal URLs are https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08664v1, and https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08664v1. Retrieval occurred on 2026-10-07 UTC after current-literature searches. The abstract page reports submission on 9 March 2026; the PDF is dated 10 March. The web tool reports 62 pages and 4,580 extracted lines. These searches did not surface a later resolving primary result; this is not an exhaustive absence theorem.

Complete retained PDF-text units are: normal/weight/cycle/PA/divisor definitions L443–562; normal-lift invariance L563–624; complete refinement Lemma 2.34 L625–762; PCC/PC definitions L880–902; complete PA/PC Lemma 3.4 L903–1001; strictness Definition 3.8 and Remark 3.9 L1064–1077; growth Definition 3.14 L1119–1122; printed regularizable Definition 3.23 L1290–1292; raw PA MA Definition 4.4 L1955–1967; complete factorial Proposition 4.12 L2148–2183; envelope Definition 6.2 L3379–3386; orthogonality Definition 6.9 L3480–3485; and complete Example 6.24, Claim 6.25, Remarks 6.26–6.27 L3979–4031. The coverage program verifies all 13 contiguous intervals without missing lines. Positive-recession Definition 4.15 was read in the fixed HTML. Theorem 4.13 was inspected only in fragments and is not applied.

Imported conventions distinguish integral slopes/rational constants from arbitrary real coefficients on finite rational structures. Normals point inward in primitive saturated tangent quotients. Finite PA MA is the raw recursive divisor, without an additional factorial. The real parameter family uses only the real-linear extension of that identical finite formula. The new theorem independently establishes all lattice, balancing, convexity, envelope, regularizable-endpoint, and mass premises. No BFJ, CLD, delta-form, analytic realization, or toric Riemann–Roch dependency is imported.

The essential extracted PCC glyph resolves to tau being a face of each sigma_i. Contact glyphs are ordinary grouping parentheses. The dossier’s printed cross obstacle gives +epsilon and -epsilon at its shared origin, so it is not continuous as written and is unused. Strict PCC tests must discard zero-coefficient terms; counting those endpoints would make the printed strict condition impossible. The new result instead proves explicit strict local affine supports. Weak PC is unchanged.

Shell curl failed with exit code 7 through the existing proxy; no settings were changed and no original PDF bytes were acquired. Actual web responses were retained as UTF-8 JSON. sources/pdf-open-and-search.json has 30,657 bytes and SHA-256 772a1a0fae5129cb1afbc6c8832f2c44d054e148082b22d92560d7c84df79704. sources/read-units-5.json has 20,128 bytes and SHA-256 a99f2be49aecdbcae29e3cd9e50bbe14546ec6bcbd674122a88c1324e7da6b40. The actual input has 62,928 bytes and SHA-256 7bec5163f730a02d8789b02cf2f685f74382691013181d1ada8218e3ef371dcf. None is an original-PDF hash.

The quote-free source-application-ledger.md records exact hypotheses and applications; execution-requests.md records actual searches and commands. evidence/source-provenance.json records retained-file hashes and coverage. notes.summary: New scoped strict-growth obstruction on the U(3,4) Bergman fan: an exact genuine integral PA envelope has masses 4,3,3 and contact integral −4ε for a strictly convex coercive reference. A parameter family and independent literal-regularity failure are proved. General P05.2 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: On the unit-weight fine U(3,4) fan, define h=max(a,b) on every pair cone, eta=|a-b| on cones 12 and 34 and max(a,b) elsewhere, and the continuous integral roof uε=(ε−min(a,b))₊ on those two cones and ε elsewhere, with rational ε>0. For A≥0, B>0, C>B, S=A+B, reference Γ=Aη+Bh and obstacle U=Cuε, the exact envelope is P=Γ+Buε. The reference has strict local supports and positive recession slopes. Raw MA(P)=4S²δ0+B(4A+3B)(δεe12+δεe34), and the contact integral is −4(C−B)εS². Integral parameters give genuine literal PA endpoints. A=0,B=1,C=2 gives masses 4,3,3, degree ten and integral −4ε. This excludes simultaneous real all-obstacle regularity and universal contact without assuming real regularity. Separately, a radial literal obstacle has a nonintegral envelope uniformly separated from literal convex PA approximants, proving literal regularity fails for h. No literal regularizable MA is assigned to that second endpoint.
notes.text:
This is an independently proved scoped obstruction, not a complete original classification. Full arguments are retained in argument.md and the standalone P05.2-paper.tex and P05.2-paper.pdf.

Conventions. Let N=Z³, e1=(1,0,0), e2=(0,1,0), e3=(0,0,1), e4=(-1,-1,-1), and eij=ei+ej. Let X be the union of the six cones sigma_ij=R≥0 ei+R≥0 ej. Subdivide each at eij, obtaining twelve fine two-dimensional cones, all of weight one. Tangent lattices are saturated. Normals point inward and represent primitive tangent-quotient generators. For a PA function f and balanced cycle c, the raw divisor coefficient is

(f·c)(tau)=Σsigma>tau c(sigma)f_sigma(n_sigma/tau)−f_tau(Σsigma>tau c(sigma)n_sigma/tau).

In dimension two MA_poly(f)=f·(f·[X]), with no further factorial. Alexandrov area is lattice-normalized subgradient area without a factorial. PA_Z has integral slopes and rational constants; PA_R has arbitrary real affine coefficients on a finite rational structure. The envelope uses all PC competitors q≤Γ+U with q≤Γ+O(1), not merely integral-slope competitors. Every measured endpoint below is already PA and has a constant decreasing regularizing sequence.

Geometry. Any three of the ei form a Z-basis. Thus (ei,ej), and consequently (ei,eij), generate their full saturated tangent lattices. At singleton ray ei use normals ej for j≠i: their sum is −ei. At pair ray eij use normals ei,ej: their sum is eij. This proves balancing. Under N=Z⁴/Z(1,1,1,1), the support consists of vectors whose minimum coordinate is attained at least twice. The uniform rank-three matroid on four elements has the full ground set as its sole circuit; its proper nonempty flats are singletons and pairs. Its circuit condition and flat chains therefore give exactly this support and fine fan. This establishes the U(3,4) description directly. The proved package is this matroidal fan geometry with saturated unimodular cones, not an unspecified stronger smoothness hypothesis.

Local-support lemma. A continuous function with an ambient affine local support at every point is convex on every segment contained in X. Indeed, subtract the segment chord. A positive maximum would have a nonempty closed maximum set inside the open segment. At a maximum, a local supporting slope must be zero by testing both directions, and the supporting inequality makes the maximum set open. Connectedness contradicts the zero endpoint values. For a PCC centered at x, its segments [x,xi] lie in X. Segment convexity propagates the local supporting slope ℓ to give f(xi)≥f(x)+ℓ(xi−x). Weighted summation proves PC. If a support agrees along tau, the divisor formula becomes Σc(sigma)(f_sigma−ℓ)(n_sigma/tau)≥0: balancing cancels the tangent correction. Thus the functions constructed below also satisfy the source’s intersection-positive PAPC definition. Changing normal lifts cancels by the same argument. In our dimension-two calculations, refinement adds zero contributions inside affine cells, preserves existing bent-edge coefficients, and gives cancelling slopes at inserted vertices on affine cycle edges; hence the raw measure is unchanged.

Functions. Fix rational ε>0. For x=a ei+b ej, a,b≥0, put h(x)=max(a,b) on every cone. Let the exceptional pairs be 12 and 34. Put eta(x)=|a−b| on exceptional cones and max(a,b) otherwise. Put uε(x)=(ε−min(a,b))₊ on exceptional cones and ε otherwise. These formulas agree at all shared rays and at zero. They are continuous literal PA on finite rational structures, and 0≤uε≤ε. The function h is the restriction of the ambient convex norm max_i zi−min_i zi on R⁴/R(1,1,1,1).

Theorem. For real A≥0, B>0, C>B, set S=A+B, Γ=A eta+B h and U=C uε. Then Γ is strictly convex relative to the fine fan, in the explicit local-support sense, and positive at infinity. Its exact envelope is

PΓ(U)=P=Γ+B uε.

Its genuine finite PA raw measure is

MA_poly,R(P)=4S²δ0+B(4A+3B)(δεe12+δεe34),

and its exact contact integral is −4(C−B)εS²<0. For integral A,B,C, all reference, obstacle and endpoint coefficients are literal, and the same measure is exactly the source’s literal finite PA operator. The real statement extends only that identical finite divisor formula real-linearly; it does not presume a general operator on nonregularizable PC functions.

Convexity and strictness. Both h and eta are convex on each coarse cone. Near r ei, let j be its exceptional partner and k,l the other indices. The germ of eta is ambient affine with values (1,−1,0,0) on (ei,ej,ek,el); the values sum to zero. At zero eta≥0 gives a zero support. Pair-ray neighborhoods lie in their coarse plane, where the convex formulas give supports. Thus the local-support lemma proves eta is PC; h is ambient convex.

At r ei, Γ has longitudinal slope S and transverse slopes −A,0,0. The ambient form with values S,−A−B/3,−B/3,−B/3 agrees along the ray and has strict transverse slack B/3. At exceptional pair rays the convex bend is 2A+B>0, and elsewhere it is S>0; averaging the two gradients gives strict supports. At zero Γ≥Bh>0 away from zero gives a strict zero support. These supports prove strictness on every proper fine face and the strict Jensen test after discarding zero-coefficient terms. Conicality and Γ≥Bh give positive slope in every nonzero recession direction.

On an exceptional cone,

P=max{Γ,Bε+S|a−b|};

on the other cones P=Bε+S max(a,b). Therefore P is convex on each coarse cone. Near r ei it is ambient affine with values (S,−S,0,0). Its origin germ is Bε+S eta, supported by the constant Bε. All other points have plane supports from the convex formulas. Hence P is PC and intersection-positive. Split each exceptional ordered half-cone a≥b at b=ε, and interchange a,b for the other half. Keep the fine cones elsewhere. This gives sixteen top cells and exactly three vertices: 0, εe12 and εe34. The structure is rational, and coefficients are integral for integral A,B. Finally P−Γ=B uε is bounded and P≤Γ+U, so P is a valid PA competitor and regularizable endpoint.

Envelope maximality against every competitor. Let q be any PC competitor. The opposite rational points εe12 and εe34 have obstacle value Bε, so q(0)≤Bε. On singleton rays q(r ei)≤Sr+Cε. Combining zero with R ei, for rational R>r, and letting R→∞ gives q(r ei)≤Sr+Bε. The identical bound holds on every nonexceptional pair ray. On an exceptional pair ray, joining zero to εeij gives q(r eij)≤Bε for 0≤r≤ε; for r≥ε the obstacle gives q(r eij)≤Br.

For a rational point in an exceptional cone with a≥b and d=a−b, use, for rational 0<θ<1,

a ei+b ej=θ(d/θ)ei+(1−θ)(b/(1−θ))eij.

If b<ε, choose θ small enough that b/(1−θ)≤ε. The ray bounds give q(x)≤Sd+Bε=P(x). If b≥ε, they give q(x)≤Sd+Bb+θBε; letting θ↓0 gives q(x)≤Sd+Bb=P(x). Diagonal and boundary points are already covered. In a nonexceptional half-cone both ray bounds are Sr+Bε, and the same combination yields q(x)≤S max(a,b)+Bε=P(x). Thus q≤P at all rational points. For an arbitrary irrational point, choose shrinking rational simplices in its relative rational face containing it. Their barycentric combinations are PCCs after rational subdivision. Applying the rational bound at their vertices and continuity of P gives q≤P there too. Consequently P is the exact envelope over all competitors. It is continuous, so upper-semicontinuous regularization changes nothing. No regularization theorem or all-obstacle regularity antecedent is hidden here.

Raw masses. For a conical function on the fine fan, write ai=f(ei), bij=f(eij). The chosen primitive normals give singleton first-divisor weight Σj≠i bij−2ai and pair weight ai+aj−bij. At a vertex the second divisor sums weights times outgoing slopes; constants contribute nothing.

The origin germ of P is Bε+S eta. It has ai=S, exceptional bij=0, and other bij=S. Its first cycle has zero singleton weights, exceptional weights 2S, and other pair weights S. It is balanced because e12+e34=0 and the remaining four pair vectors sum to zero. Exceptional slopes are zero, other pair slopes S, yielding mass 4S².

At p=εe12 use the saturated plane basis e1,e2 and local coordinates x,y. Removing Bε, the active gradients are (S,−A),(−A,S),(S,−S),(−S,S). The primitive local first-cycle rays are (1,1),(−1,−1),(1,0),(0,1), their weights respectively 2A+B,2S,B,B, and their outgoing slopes B,0,S,S. The weights balance since (2A+B)(1,1)+2S(−1,−1)+B(1,0)+B(0,1)=0. On the positive diagonal, inward normals (1,0),(0,1) give slope sum 2S minus tangent slope B; on the negative diagonal the tangent slope is zero; opposing normal differences on the axes are B. The second mass is B(2A+B)+2BS=B(4A+3B). The other special vertex is identical. There are no other vertices, hence no other atoms. These are all vertex balances of the global first cycle, whose open edges are straight weighted lines.

The ordered gradient polygon (S,−S),(S,−A),(−A,S),(−S,S) has shoelace area B(4A+3B)/2. The subdifferential is its convex hull: supporting inequalities give inclusion, while separation and a directional test exclude points outside. Thus the raw atom is exactly 2! times the lattice-normalized Alexandrov area. No ambient Alexandrov measure is substituted for the singular origin.

For Γ, first weights are B at each singleton, 2A+B at exceptional pairs and S elsewhere. Its raw degree is 4BS+2B(2A+B)+4S²=4A²+16AB+10B². P has equal total mass 4S²+2B(4A+3B). However P−(Γ+U)=(B−C)uε, equal to (B−C)ε at zero and zero at both other atoms. Therefore the contact integral is exactly −4(C−B)εS². In particular A=0,B=1,C=2 gives Γ=h, U=2uε, P=h+uε, raw masses 4,3,3, degree ten and integral −4ε, entirely with literal coefficients.

Separate literal-regularity failure. For Γ=h and integer n≥2, define the bounded literal obstacle vn=min{1/n,(1−h)₊}. Its exact envelope is Qn=max{h,(1−1/n)h+1/n}. This candidate is ambient convex, differs boundedly from h, and lies below h+vn because on h≤1 its gap (1−h)/n is at most both 1/n and 1−h. Every competitor has q(0)≤1/n and q(y)≤1 when h(y)=1. For rational x with 0<h(x)≤1, the radial PCC from zero to y=x/h(x) gives q(x)≤(1−h(x))/n+h(x). Outside h≥1 the obstacle is h; rational simplices finish the bound at other points.

On the primitive segment r e1, 0≤r≤1, Qn has slope 1−1/n. A literal convex PA approximant ψ has nondecreasing integral slopes. Let k be its right-hand midpoint slope and δ its uniform error. If k≥1, its right-half increment is at least 1/2, giving 2δ≥1/(2n). If k≤0, its left-half increment is at most zero, giving 2δ≥(1−1/n)/2≥1/(2n). Thus δ≥1/(4n). Literal uniform regularization is impossible. No literal regularizable MA is assigned to Qn; this does not affect the genuine literal PA measure of h+uε.

Scope and failed methods. The result establishes a strictly convex, positive-growth, saturated matroidal fan obstruction with an actual PA endpoint, extending the flat-reference mechanism in the supplied context. It does not establish real regularity for every obstacle on this fan, classify general pairs, or disprove a stronger unspecified intrinsic smoothness condition. The simplest literal pair fails regularity separately; the real pair cannot have both all-obstacle regularity and universal contact. An ambient-volume contact argument fails to account for singular raw mass: the origin envelope is flat along its exceptional two-sided line but has positive top intersection mass. A changing-reference continuity strategy would require a common justified operator domain and local continuity, so it was abandoned in favor of the exact formula.

Artifacts contain full hypotheses, proofs, source applications and evidence: P05.2-paper.tex, P05.2-paper.pdf, argument.md, source-application-ledger.md and structured-notes.json. The full original P05.2 necessary-and-sufficient characterization remains open.

notes.detailedSummary: The Fraction program checks all twelve cone saturation cases, vertex balances, raw masses, degree identities and special polygon areas for four rational parameter tuples. It exhausts 4,056 prescribed point checks and 7,200 midpoint checks. These finite results do not certify continuum or analytic claims; n2 supplies independent proofs. Source coverage passed all 13 pertinent intervals. The final nine-page PDF compiled without warnings. No installation or resource-heavy computation was used, and no supervised service or runtime model change is claimed.
notes.text:
Deliverables are P05.2-paper.tex, P05.2-paper.pdf, argument.md, source-application-ledger.md, execution-requests.md, structured-notes.json, check_obstruction.py, obstruction-input.json, source_provenance.py, build_notes.py, README.md, sources/ retrieval records and evidence/ outputs. The final PDF has nine pages; pdflatex exited zero with no warnings or overfull boxes. Compilation and visual inspection establish artifact usability, not mathematical correctness.

The finite program uses Python 3.12.14 standard-library Fraction arithmetic. Parameter tuples (A,B,C,ε) are (0,1,2,1), (2,1,2,1), (1/3,2/5,7/6,3/2), and (1,1/10,1,1/4). All twelve fine-cone saturation cases passed. Every triple of distinct ei has determinant of absolute value one. The program checks conical divisor weights, all vertex balances, second masses and polygon areas exactly.

Outputs ordered as (degree, origin mass, each special mass, each special Alexandrov area, contact integral) are (10,4,3,3/2,−4); (58,36,11,11/2,−36); (188/45,484/225,76/75,38/75,−2783/1125); and (57/10,121/25,43/100,43/200,−1089/1000). All assertions passed.

Per tuple, point tests use a,b in {kε/4:k=0,…,12} on six cones, giving 6·13²=1,014 checks. Midpoint tests use all unordered distinct pairs among the 25 points (kε/2,lε/2), k,l=0,…,4, on six cones, giving 6·binom(25,2)=1,800 checks. Across four tuples, all 4,056 point checks and 7,200 midpoint checks passed. Exhaustiveness concerns these finite lists only; envelope maximality and continuum convexity follow from n2’s proofs, not computation.

The provenance program reported 13 complete source-unit intervals, 12 actual hashed files, no missing lines, and no claimed original-PDF hash. The environment is Linux 6.18.44-x86_64 with glibc 2.41 and pdfTeX 1.40.26 from TeX Live 2025/dev/Debian. Detailed outputs are evidence/check-output.json, evidence/environment.json, evidence/source-provenance.json, evidence/latex-final.stdout, P05.2-paper.log and evidence/deliverable-check.json. Rerun from this directory: python check_obstruction.py; python source_provenance.py; python build_notes.py; pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error P05.2-paper.tex twice. Registered supportingNoteIds in the structured artifact use only n1, n2 and n3.

No installation or resource-heavy computation was used. No supervised compute service was exposed or needed; no runtime model change is claimed. The exact established scope is a higher-dimensional strict-growth obstruction with genuine measured PA endpoints, plus literal nonregularity for its simplest reference. The general structural characterization for all balanced rational polyhedral pairs, actual references and admissible obstacles remains unsolved. All notes are unverified drafts. Candidate=false.
